subject.title: update: immutable release roots to eliminate multi-minute gateway downtime on git deploys

question: Should OpenClaw adopt immutable release roots as the supported architecture for managed git updates, including the operational cost of release retention, garbage collection, and supervisor integration?
rationale: This is a product and operations architecture decision, not a bounded repair: it changes how managed installations are laid out, switched, recovered, and rolled back across supported platforms.

options.title: Sponsor phased release-root updates
options.body: Define the canonical release-root and service-switch contract, then implement it behind focused updater and supervisor milestones.

options.title: Keep in-place updates
options.body: Retain the existing update model and accept build-duration gateway downtime while documenting its operational tradeoff.

options.title: Limit the scope first
options.body: Adopt only preflight improvements now and defer immutable roots until the supported supervisor and rollback contract is agreed.

recommendation.title: Sponsor phased release-root updates
recommendation.body: Define the canonical release-root and service-switch contract, then implement it behind focused updater and supervisor milestones.

likelyOwner.reason: The reporter supplied the concrete deployment evidence and the proposed cross-cutting architecture, making them the clearest available routing candidate pending ownership confirmation.
